title: sse-token-anchor-and-escape-synchronizer-for-robust-partial-json-resume
author: Ava Fernandez
release_notes: Fixes multiple SSE framing edge-cases: stabilizes partial-JSON reassembly across chunk boundaries, avoids delimiter-escape collisions, and reduces ordering-induced fncall/tool-call regressions. No API surface change.
description:
Context and motivation:
Streaming endpoints were occasionally emitting partial JSON objects when clients received mid-JSON chunk boundaries combined with delimiter bytes split across TCP frames or UTF-8 multi-byte characters broken by the framing layer. This caused downstream OpenAI-compat clients and tool/function call routers to mis-parse structured output or drop function-call sentinel events. The problem surface is intermittent and correlated with bursty backpressure and proxy reassembly timing.

What this PR does (single description):
- Introduces a lightweight token-anchor scheme for SSE frames: each outbound 'data:' chunk includes an anchor header (anchor-id + offset-ms) that allows the receiver reassembler to prefer stable cut points when reassembling partial JSON spans. Anchors are soft hints used for reassembly heuristics rather than strict sequence numbers to avoid coupling across heterogeneous transports.
- Adds an escape-sanitizer pass that detects delimiter sequences ("

", separator tokens, and function-call sentinels) that may be split across chunk boundaries or split inside multi-byte UTF-8 sequences and rewrites them into safe, idempotent escape tokens which the reassembler then unescapes once a complete JSON span is reconstructed.
- Tightens the reassembly window and introduces a small checksum (64-bit truncated) over the last N bytes of a span to detect accidental recombination that would produce invalid JSON. On checksum mismatch the stream emits a resync marker and tries an ordered replay iteration.
- Improves the OpenAI-compat adapter to treat function-call sentinel events as atomic when anchors indicate continuity; this reduces fncall ordering regression when a function payload crosses a chunk boundary.
- Extensive new unit/integration tests and a fuzz harness simulating chunk splits at UTF-8 codepoint boundaries, delimiter-splitting, and proxy-induced reorder.

Commits (high-level):

- 2) escape sanitizer and sanitizer tests (services/stream/sanitizer.go + services/stream/sanitizer_test.go)
- 3) reassembly checksum + resync markers (services/stream/reassembler.go + protocol/markers.go)
- 4) openai-compat adapter updates to treat anchored fncalls as atomic (api/openai/compat/stream_adapter.go)
- 5) integration and fuzz harness (tests/stream/fuzz_split_chunks.go + tests/integration/openai_stream_scenarios.md)

Testing and CI: 
- Local unit tests: all pass. Added ~120 assertions across sanitizer/reassembler.
- Integration: ran the openai-compat streaming scenario suite with a synthetic proxy that injects chunk splits; observed deterministic repro previously failing tests now passing.
- Fuzz runs: 2x 30-minute local fuzz sessions; discovered and fixed edgecases for certain 4-byte emoji sequences split at the second byte.
- CI history: initial CI run failed (one flaky integration test due to timing). I added a short-poll backoff and retried. Final CI run passed: build | lint | unit | integration | fuzz-smoke => pass.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Marcus Lee: "Can we avoid adding too much per-chunk overhead on the hot path? I'm worried about the additional header bytes and checksum cost for the 99th percentile of short responses."
- Ava (author): "Anchor header is tiny (8-12 bytes), checksum uses DMA-friendly xxhash64 and is optional when payload < 256 bytes; we gate via metrics and operator flags. Benchmarks below show <2% p99 token latency impact for our test corpus."
- Marcus Lee: "Please add a feature flag and document fallback semantics."
- Ava: "Added sse.escape_sanitizer_enabled and sse.anchor_window_ms with default safe values in config docs; documented fallback to resync markers."
- Priya Nair: "Integration looks good; can you add a test that simulates repeated partial JSON fragments arriving out of order?"
- Ava: "Added reassembler_test.go case 'out_of_order_replay' that exercises the checksum+resync path."
